newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus wins big USAir order - paper.
newsitem.headline: Airbus wins big USAir order - paper.

text.p: Airbus Industrie has won a firm order for 120 A319 and A320 planes from USAir, the Wall Street Journal Europe said in a report citing people familiar with the deal.
While list prices for the planes would be $5.3 billion, Airbus used "aggressive" discounts to win the order from the Pittsburg-based airline over rival Boeing Co.

The WSJE said a preliminary purchase agreement is expected to be signed this week. The paper said USAir would also take options for 120 to 180 planes which could take the deal to over $12 billion at list prices.
Deliveries are expected to begin in 1998.
The paper said Airbus, Boeing and USAir had no comment.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
